messages:
kube-audit-bot: ALERT: Image signature mismatch for pod redwood-staging-api-7f4b in ns=staging on node=staging-node-3. Image digest registry.redwood.com/api@sha256:abcd1234 does not match signed digest. Possible tampering. Detected hostPath mount to /proc in container. link: https://alerts.internal/redwood/1830001234

maria.g: seeing this now, thanks. Is this the canary deploy from last night?

devon: Not from our pipeline AFAIK. CI job `canary-deploy/staging` ran 03:12 UTC but used digest sha256:abcd1234 which doesn't match signed digest. Pulling image manifest now.

samir: I'm cordoning the node. Command: `kubectl cordon staging-node-3 && kubectl drain staging-node-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

security-oncall: +1 isolate the node. Also please `kubectl delete pod redwood-staging-api-7f4b -n staging`. Rotate any service account tokens that were mounted in that pod: `kubectl delete secret kafka-svc-token-...`

devon: grabbing manifest and container logs:
``
$ kubectl -n staging logs redwood-staging-api-7f4b -c app
2026-03-18T03:18:12Z start
...open shell...
sh: cannot set terminal process group: Inappropriate ioctl for device
/ # ls -la /proc/1/root
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root 0 Mar 18 03:18 /proc/1/root -> /
```

maria.g: that looks like an interactive shell. Was hostPID allowed on this pod? It shouldn't be.

samir: checking pod spec: `securityContext.hostPID: true` — how did that get applied? Not in our deployment manifests.

nima: I see a `ClusterRoleBinding` created at 03:15 UTC by `system:serviceaccount:ci:runner-sa` with role `cluster-admin`. Audit log shows `kubectl create clusterrolebinding` from IP 34.56.78.90. Suspect CI runner compromise.

jen: filing INC-3421, adding initial evidence and timeline. Assigning to infra/security.

security-oncall: Actions: 1) revoke CI runner SA tokens and delete clusterrolebinding 2) isolate node + collect forensic tarball (logs, /var/log/pods, containerd) 3) delete pod and block image digest at the registry. samir: you handle node isolation. devon: collect image manifest and registry audit. maria.g: notify product owners and SRE.

samir: node cordoned and pod deleted. Collecting tarball to s3://rdwf-incidents/1830001234/ (forensic in progress).

devon: registry shows a push at 03:10 UTC from IP 34.56.78.90 with username `ci-bot`. Token used was rotated yesterday. Disabling that token and revoking any matching service account tokens now. We'll also rotate the KMS key used to encrypt deploy secrets — note: rotating KMS key will require re-encrypting secrets and a small maintenance window.

maria.g: also need to update RBAC: remove cluster-admin from `ci` namespace SA and create a least-privilege role for the deployer. Add a CI policy review.

security-oncall: agreed. Post-incident action items: full audit log export, revoke compromised keys, rotate registry credentials, disable affected KMS key version, create detection rule for hostPID + image signature mismatch, update CI manifests and add automated manifest signing. Samir to lead forensic write-up, Jen to author the postmortem and timeline.

jen: postmortem doc created: https://docs.internal/redwood/sec/postmortems/INC-3421. Adding timeline, evidence links, and remediation owners.

kube-audit-bot: Evidence bundle uploaded: s3://rdwf-incidents/1830001234/evidence.tar.gz

security-oncall: Thanks team. We'll run a 1-hour postmortem at 13:00 UTC and review KMS rotation window. Closing slack thread — follow-ups in the postmortem doc and the Jira incident ticket.
